title: A Water Drop Magnifier
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: turn a single drop of water into a magnifying lens that makes letters look bigger.

body.heading: Make the lens
paragraphs: Put a clear plastic lid over some small print. Ask your adult to place one round drop of water in the middle of the lid, right over a word.
Look down through the drop. The letters underneath look bigger. Your drop of water is working as a magnifying lens.

body.heading: Why it works
paragraphs: The drop is curved like a tiny hill. Light bends as it passes through the curve, and the bend makes things look larger than they are.
Real magnifying glasses work the same way. They are made of curved glass instead of water, but the bending trick is identical.

body.heading: Drop detective work
paragraphs: Try a bigger drop and a smaller drop. Which one makes the letters look biggest? A flatter drop bends light less than a tall, round one.
When you finish, tip the water away. Your amazing science tool was just one drop of water all along.

takeaway: A curved drop of water bends light like a magnifying glass and makes small things look bigger.
safetyNotes: An adult should help with the water. Keep water away from books that must not get wet — use an old newspaper.
screenFreeExtension: Look at other tiny things through your drop — a grain of rice, a seed, or the lines on your fingertip.
